fields.Text:
Which herpesvirus remains latent in mononuclear cells (e.g., macrophages)?

{{c1::CMV}}
fields.Extra:
Latent in mononuclear cells (Not B or T cells though. EBV is just B cells)

Location of Latency
HSV-1Trigeminal nerve ganglion
HSV-2Sacral nerve ganglion
VZVDorsal root or trigeminal ganglia
EBVB-cells
CMVMyeloid (monocytes & macrophages)

This card used to say CMV remains latent in B and T cells; according to multiple sources it actually remains latent in mononuclear myeloid cells (Nov 2024)


- Latency: the productive cycle is off, but it can be reactivated

fields.Text: After primary infection, stress can reactivate HSV-1, which can result in {{c2::herpes labialis (cold sores)}}
fields.Extra:
- Most common viral infection of the mouth

- Remains dormant in the trigeminal ganglion

- After 2-3 weeks, initial infection resolves and the virus can enter sensory nerve endings and establish latency in the trigeminal ganglion or other sensory ganglia through axonal transport

- Viral reactivation can occur due to stress and lead to conditions such as herpetic labialis (cold sores around the mouth), gingivostomatitis, or keratoconjunctivitis




- The reactivated virus comes back down the axon and replicates in the epithelium

fields.Text: When compared to HCV, HBV is {{c1::less}} likely to become a chronic infection

- In HBV, only 5 - 10% of adult cases develop chronic infection; younger children are at higher risk

- In HCV, infections become chronic in 60 - 80% of cases

- The most common outcome of HBV infection is acute hepatitis with mild symptoms that fully resolves in > 95% of cases

- In adults HBV is usually acute and cleared in about six months

fields.Text: Antigenic shift is associated with {{c2::pan}}demics
fields.Extra:
- Pandemics span over continents/worldwide
- HA and NA undergo antigenic variation which allow for outbreaks resistant to previous vaccination
- Influenza viruses are named based on HA and NA types example H1N1

- Antigenic shift is the exchange of RNA segments between animal and human viruses which cause new HA or NA leading to pandemics
- Antigenic drift is the spontaneous mutation that create slightly altered HA or NA leading to epidemics


- Pandemic strains kill millions, seasonal strains much less
